pages.answerEvidence: Readable timing with broken letters can indicate that caption bytes were interpreted using the wrong character encoding. Preserve the original, compare the text in a trusted editor and player, and confirm its actual encoding before converting. Missing glyphs and incorrect translation are different problems; a video quality change cannot repair them.

pages.answerEvidence: The source player can draw captions from a separate text resource that is not inside the video stream. A downloaded video can therefore preserve pictures and sound while lacking that overlay. SocialVidDownloader currently selects source video and audio; it does not promise subtitle export or every text track offered by the source platform.

pages.answerEvidence: Treat automatic captions as draft text that needs checking against the recording. Review names, numbers, negations, speaker changes, and meaningful sounds before relying on instructions or sharing the text. A fluent sentence can still misrepresent what was said. Downloading the media does not certify the caption wording or generate a verified transcript.
